before_board.S: A Kakeya set K in F_q^n.

bound_then: TWO REGIMES, neither dominating: |K| >~ q^{(n+2)/2} (verified; best known for small n) and a high-dimensional arithmetic improvement whose exponent P1 gives as 4n/7 (DISPUTED — see correction). See bound_regimes.
leak: Cauchy-Schwarz sees pairwise line interactions only, which caps the exponent near n/2.

sources_before.tier: SEARCH (search snippets; no PDF fetched in this container)
sources_before.basis: Row C5-wolff verifies q^{(n+2)/2} as the finite-field benchmark for Besicovitch sets.

sources_before.debt: the seed wrote about q^{4n/7} with low confidence; not fetched
sources_before.basis: Row C5-4n7 is DISPUTED: 4n/7 + 3/7 is Katz-Tao's EUCLIDEAN Minkowski-dimension bound and no source reached here states it for |K| in F_q^n. The two-regime structure survives; the exponent does not.

bound_regimes.valid_range: exceeds Wolff only for n >= 15; the two are equal at n = 14
bound_regimes.dispute: Katz-Tao's 4n/7 + 3/7 is a lower bound on the MINKOWSKI DIMENSION of Kakeya sets in R^n — the Euclidean problem. No source reached this session states an exponent 4n/7 for |K| in F_q^n. Finite-field improvements over (n+2)/2 do exist in dimensions >= 5 (Katz-Tao; Mockenhaupt-Tao 2004), so the two-regime STRUCTURE survives, but this exponent is not verified for the finite field.

leaks.evidence: The bush argument double-counts incidences and uses no structure in the direction set; Cauchy-Schwarz sees pairwise line interactions only.
leaks.ranking: leading for this regime (blind encoder, L2)

leaks.evidence: Bourgain-Katz-Tao supplies only a qualitative sum-product exponent, so the gain is not quantitative.
leaks.ranking: leading for this regime (blind encoder, L2)

correction.was: |K| >~ q^{(n+2)/2}, later about q^{4n/7} — ordered as though 4n/7 superseded Wolff
correction.why: (n+2)/2 > 4n/7 exactly when n < 14; they meet at n = 14. No single exponent dominated uniformly at the 2008 cutoff. The two regimes leak differently, so a single-regime bound field forced a single leak where there are two.

second_error.what: Beyond the ordering error L2 found, the high-dimensional exponent itself appears to import a Euclidean Minkowski-dimension bound into a finite-field cardinality bound.
second_error.consequence: The n < 14 crossover in tools/check_corrections.py is correct AS ARITHMETIC on the two exponents as P1 writes them, but if 4n/7 is not the finite-field exponent then the crossover POINT is an artefact. The two-regime finding that motivated the schema change does not depend on the crossover point.
